items.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said he expected the Bills offense to be “more complex” in Week 12 against the Chiefs.
items.text: Fowler suggested the Bills kept the game plan as simple as possible last week against the inferior Dolphins, with Josh Allen throwing 45 passes from the pocket and failing to log a single rushing attempt after averaging 7.1 rushes per game coming into Week 11. Fowler said the Bills might have wanted to hide offensive wrinkles ahead of their Thanksgiving night matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. items.title: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo said it “sounds like” the benching of Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph was “not a popular decision in the locker room.”
items.text: Rodgers was reportedly excused from meetings at the team facility on Wednesday, two days ahead of the Steelers’ Week 12 game against Denver. Rodgers’ benching comes after a series of down games and a proposed change from Rodgers about how plays are communicated to him during the game. Rudolph could be a slight upgrade for Pittsburgh pass catchers and should be rostered in supeflex formats for now. - Denny Carter

items.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Rodgers was excused from a Wednesday morning meeting.
items.text: Schefter said the veteran was excused from showing up Wednesday morning so he could “process” being benched in favor of Mason Rudolph for Week 12 against the Broncos. That seems fair. Whatever happens from here, Rodgers has certainly taken his last snap as a Steeler. Rudolph, meanwhile, should be rostered in all superflex leagues for now. - Denny Carter

items.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy made the decision to bench Aaron Rodgers.
items.text: Rapoport said McCarthy’s decision came after extensive meetings with coaches, players, and Rodgers himself following the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Joe Milton-led Eagles. Mason Rudolph is slated to get the start in Week 12 against the Broncos. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo said the team was set to make a change in play calling, with QB coach Tom Arth relaying plays to Rodgers on game days “at the behest of Rodgers.” Hours later, the 42-year-old veteran was benched. items.title: The Steelers have named Mason Rudolph their starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
items.text: The news of Aaron Rodgers’ benching and Rudolph’s sudden promotion came in an 11:10 PM ET Tuesday evening press release. Normal stuff. While we wait for the next shoe to drop on the “Rodgers situation,” we can begin evaluating the “Rudolph development.” In short: Not much will change, though Rodgers’ recent immobility and subsequent inaccuracy had reached a boiling point. Rudolph will oversee an attack that figures to make a sudden swerve to the run, though the 31-year-old with 742 career pass attempts should be able to keep a wideout or two afloat in deeper fantasy leagues. items.title: The Steelers have announced they are benching Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph named the starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
items.text: 42-year-old Rodgers’ play had taken a sudden, dramatic turn for the worse of late, but it’s still a stunning announcement, especially since it came via a terse team statement. It also comes one day after coach Mike McCarthy claimed he was not considering turning to one of his myriad other QB options (the team also has second-year pro Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar on the 53-man roster). Other information is scarce, except for the statement including Rodgers would be inactive for the Friday afternoon contest. items.title: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports there have “not been a lot of talks about an extension in-season” for Bryce Young.
items.text: Wolfe adds that Young and the Panthers are “on the same page for an offseason contract.” Young started out strong this season before a three-turnover loss to the Buccaneers in Week 7. The Panthers are still in first place atop the NFC South with a 5-5 record and a second bout with the Bucs on the horizon for Week 12. Young’s extension chances were highly reliant on his play this season but the Panthers need to see more before committing to the 25-year-old quarterback. items.title: Alex Highsmith (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
items.text: Highsmith suffered an ankle injury in Week 11 and starts out the week not practicing. He was wearing an ankle brace in the team facility on Tuesday and head coach Mike McCarthy said it will be “tough” for Highsmith to play in a shortened Week 12 where the Steelers play the Broncos on Friday. Highsmith is trending in the wrong direction this week, but his ankle issue does not seem to be a major injury. - Aditya Fuldeore

items.title: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
items.text: Eagles DC Vic Fangio said today he believed Mitchell would be able to go, and it seems like he’s trending in the right direction after hitting the practice field today. It would certainly help anyone facing CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens this week if Mitchell were able to go. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Dallas Goedert (shin) practiced in full on Tuesday.
items.text: That makes us feel pretty confident that he’ll suit up for Thanksgiving’s game against the Cowboys after a limited session on Monday. The Eagles’ passing game is in pretty rough shape with Joe Milton under center, but Dallas’ issues invite a TE1-capable game script for Goedert if the Eagles can take advantage of it. - Rivers McCown
